public_body: Cambridge Police Review And Advisory Board
overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by entering Purpose 1 executive session without giving complaint subjects their rights and by giving insufficient executive session topic detail in the notice and announcement; other allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged impermissible discussions with the city Law Department and related Board authority and procedure matters.
allegations.key_passage: Many of these allegations constitute matters of Board authority and procedure, and therefore we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board's executive secretary, a city employee, withheld information, misstated the mission statement, and engaged in illegal discussion.
allegations.key_passage: because the Open Meeting Law does not apply to individual employees such as Executive Secretary Corr, the allegations about Mr. Corr’s conduct, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board entered Purpose 1 executive session to discuss a complaint against a police commissioner without giving him the required notice and participation rights.
allegations.key_passage: The rights set forth in General Laws chapter 30A, section 21(a)(1), must be afforded to all subjects of complaints that the Board seeks to discuss during a Purpose 1 executive session.

allegations.summary: Meeting notice and pre-session announcement gave insufficient detail about the executive session topic (complaint review), and complaint identifiers and complainant names were withheld.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to include sufficient detail about the executive session topic, both in the notice and in the announcement at the meeting prior to entering the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board withheld information about his complaint, including failing to say it would be voted on in executive session and denying information on a visit.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, most of these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board violated its own regulations and the Cambridge municipal code.
allegations.key_passage: Our Division only has jurisdiction to evaluate Open Meeting Law violations and therefore we decline to review any allegations relating to Board regulations or municipal ordinance.

remedy: Provide each subject of the complaints discussed in the January 30, 2019 executive session with an unredacted version of the portion of the minutes concerning them.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to provide each of the subjects of the complaints that were discussed during the January 30, 2019, executive session with an unredacted version of the portion of the minutes concerning them.
